incident.what: The agent's worker pool died on provider overload (HTTP 5xx). It fell back to doing all the work inline on the most expensive model, without probing cheaper rungs: the free cloud tier (already reported dead that morning by a colleague — the agent had not read the report), a local model daemon (present, unprobed), a cheaper cloud model (untried). It also did not tell the operator which rung it was on.
incident.signal: The operator, noticing the cost, asked why no cheaper dispatch was used.

root_cause: No fallback ladder existed as a procedure; the choice was made ad hoc under time pressure.

law.text: Dispatch follows an ordered ladder and each rung is probed, not assumed: workers -> free/cheap cloud -> local model -> cheaper cloud model -> flagship inline LAST. The rung actually used, and why the higher rungs failed, is written into the round. Flagship-inline is a disclosed exception, never a silent default.
checks: each round that dispatched work names the rung used
a probe result exists for every rung skipped
colleague reports about provider status were read before choosing a rung

notes: De-identified from a real operating incident. Names, systems and paths removed; the mechanism is kept.
